---
title: "Motivating surrogate modelling"
---

## Why surrogate modelling?

Many scientific disciplines rely on computational simulators which reproduce
complex behaviours. However, these simulators are often slow and expensive to
run, making tasks like scenario analysis, forecasting and parameter inference
difficult or impractical. For example, a single forward simulation of a large
COVID-19 agent-based model like JUNE can take several days
[@chopra2023differentiableagentbasedepidemiology].

Surrogate models learn to approximate these systems from simulations that have
already been run. Once trained, they can produce new predictions much faster.
Surrogates can be built using methods such as splines and nonparametric
statistics; neural networks offer a flexible alternative for complex outputs,
including whole time series.

::: {.callout-tip}
For an overview of the surrogate modelling process and a reporting standard
for surrogates, see SMRS [@NEURIPS2025_3e1d8e89].
:::

## Introducing METIS

METIS is a Python package for training neural surrogates of time series
simulators. You supply a bank of simulator inputs and their output trajectories.
METIS provides functions to load and split that bank, train different models,
check their predictions and save a fitted surrogate for use in your own work.
You can use these functions in a script or notebook, or configure the same
training workflow through Hydra files and command-line overrides.

The walkthrough uses one stochastic epidemic model, **SIRDS**, throughout. We
first look at its simulations and how to organise them, then train several
surrogates on the same bank and use the fitted models to make new predictions.
When you bring your own simulator, the data change; the package workflow stays
the same.

::: {.callout-important}
METIS is intended to be useful without deep learning expertise, though some
familiarity with neural networks and their training will help. If you are new
to the subject or feeling rusty, these resources are useful:

* [But what is a neural network? (YouTube)](https://youtu.be/aircAruvnKk)
* [Introduction to Machine Learning (Online Notes)](https://clairedavid.github.io/intro_to_ml/nn/nn_0_intro.html)
* [Understanding Deep Learning (Textbook)](https://udlbook.github.io/udlbook/)
:::
